card.title: Procedural blob generator
card.body: A tiny tool that spits out endless organic shapes for hero backgrounds.

blocks.html: Started as a favor for a hero background and turned into its own toy. The generator layers a handful of noise-perturbed circles and blends them with a metaball-style filter to get that soft, organic blob look.
Every refresh gives a new shape, and a small control panel lets you dial in point count, wobble amount, and color. Export button spits out a clean SVG path, ready to drop into any design file.

card.title: Chat with my terminal
card.body: An LLM wired straight into my shell — mostly harmless, occasionally chaotic.

blocks.html: A background process watches my shell history and lets me ask questions in plain English — "what was that docker command from last week" — and get back a real, runnable line.
Gave it a system prompt with too much attitude, so it now refuses to help with anything before coffee. Working as intended.

card.title: Synth pad in the browser
card.body: Web Audio experiment: four oscillators, one knob, way too much reverb.

blocks.html: Four detuned oscillators feeding a single lowpass filter and a convolution reverb. One knob controls everything at once because too many knobs is how you end up never finishing a project.
Sounds best played through actual speakers, not laptop ones — you have been warned.

card.title: Tiny CLI that guesses your mood
card.body: Feed it a sentence, it feeds back a color and a bad joke.

details.title: Tiny CLI that guesses your mood

blocks.html: A single-binary CLI that scores the sentiment of whatever you type and prints back a matching color swatch plus a joke of questionable quality.
Built mostly to learn Rust. The jokes were not part of the plan but they were the part everyone liked.

card.title: ESP32 desk light rig
card.body: Ambient lighting that reacts to my calendar. Mostly reacts by turning red.

blocks.html: A strip of addressable LEDs behind the monitor polls my calendar every minute. Free time is a calm blue, meetings are amber, and back-to-back days turn the whole strip red as a warning to future me.
V2 swapped a flaky relay for a proper LED driver board — no more flickering every time the WiFi hiccups.

card.title: Emoji-only markdown parser
card.body: Because someone had to write a spec for this. That someone was bored.

blocks.html: A markdown dialect where headings, bold, and lists are all written with emoji instead of symbols. Fully spec'd, fully parsed, fully unnecessary.
The best part is the error messages, which are also emoji-only, which means they help nobody.

card.title: Voice-controlled sketch pad
card.body: Say a shape, watch it draw. Say "undo" a lot.

blocks.html: Speech recognition maps simple phrases — "circle", "bigger", "move left" — onto canvas drawing commands. Genuinely useful for quick wireframing when your hands are busy.
Undo is the most-used command by a wide margin, which tells you everything about how well the shape recognition works.

card.title: Generative playlist covers
card.body: Turns a Spotify playlist mood into a cover art palette.

blocks.html: Pulls audio features (tempo, energy, valence) for every track in a playlist and maps the averages onto a generative gradient and shape composition.
Chill playlists get soft pastel blobs, workout playlists get sharp neon triangles. Surprisingly on the nose most of the time.
